text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000018 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation at every complexity tier, but records came back for too few claims to test whether the notes support the billed levels.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern raises concern because the elevated 99215 share is not limited to sicker patients. It runs several times the all-provider rate even among patients with zero or one chronic condition. Sampled examples such as C0008337 (back pain, no chronic conditions), C0008883 and C0008934 (Z09 follow-up only) and C0008348 (isolated hypertension) are hard to reconcile with high-complexity visits. The documentation does not settle the question: only one documented 99215 claim exists (C0008680, documented as high MDM), and one of the four notes claiming moderate-or-higher data review has no lab or test line on the claim, which is weak evidence of a note-to-claim mismatch. As a first step, a reviewer should request charts specifically for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed, starting with the Z09 and single-symptom visits, and check whether the documented MDM and minutes support level 5."}
